notes.title: INERTIAL DRIFT IS EVOLVING!
notes.content:
WELCOME TO UPDATE #1!
We're really happy to announce today that big changes are coming to Inertial Drift - but before we get to that, we have to say a huge thank you to everyone who has shown support, bought, downloaded, wishlisted or reviewed Inertial drift. 

Over the past year, we've been thinking about how we can improve and grow the overall experience and today is the first day of that journey into expanding the Inertial Drift universe.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/8fe11ac0215f0572dcf6dcedad9f15a0cfe16c86.png

As some of you will have noticed there are some changes to the current roster, specifically;

- The original Roton 7D is now Class B with updated handling.
- We've also added a New upgraded Roton 7D Super for Class A.

In the coming months we will release a further three upgraded cars to the roster as well. We're currently aiming to have one added to Inertial Drift every month.

Perhaps most importantly however, we have overhauled the leaderboards. From today, there are new individual Time Attack Leaderboards for each car - it's a big move and will hopefully be the groundwork Inertial Drift needed to make this part of the game more compelling and competitive - allowing you to prove your worth with each individual car against other players globally.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/4b923c24f383d0dd4e417b4bbceb23b69a0255c7.jpg

Now that this groundwork has been completed - what are the next steps?

We're looking forward to rolling these out into next year, so please bear with us for more specific details on the roadmap - but they will include; 

- New tracks! 
- Brand new cars 
- Expanded single player content.
- Visual Improvements
- And some nice surprises!

If you're only just arriving at Inertial Drift, you'll find the game current discounted in store, so there's never been a better time to join us and find out what makes Inertial Drift so unique. We hope you enjoy your time with us and join us for the long road ahead.

Take care and all the best,
The Level 91 and PQube team.

notes.title: Inertial Drift: Development History
notes.content:
Inertial Drift has been 7 years in the making(!) - and to give you an an idea of how the game evolved into the version you see today, we wanted to showcase Inertial Drift's whole development timeline!

2013-2015
The first prototype was built in 2013 and looked like this through to 2015 while exploring how to do physics/handling. 
https://media.giphy.com/media/KVvClZMVMIFGx5Xiyl/giphy.gif

April 2016
After some contract work on another project started to wind down, development on Inertial Drift start to pick up. This is the first test track. Handling and collision are garbage, but the twin stick controls are already fun.
https://media.giphy.com/media/WxuNfPePAKpYTuWunX/giphy.gif

May 2016
The first pass on designing actual tracks. This would go on to become the first track in the game, Lakeside Loop. Handling is a lot better now.
https://media.giphy.com/media/yiQOrfNrpXiszKiUvF/giphy.gif
From above the track still looks a lot like the final version, the major features are there, things were just tightened up, refined and the final section (right most on the image) was replaced. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/c379a7a5ee910bf4d426675afd0366da508561ae.jpg

June 2016
Our very first art pass. The same layout but with some very basic texture work, terrain, shader and model replacement, but no real artstyle in mind yet.
https://media.giphy.com/media/p3jJSAAaF5GJ6hpUWk/giphy.gif

Late 2016
Our first pitch and experimenting in a very different direction visually. The handling of the four cars at this point is surprisingly close to their final iterations. Already some car animation work going on here, but much more of that to come.
https://media.giphy.com/media/qUfpYasjWQDDRgxmzh/giphy.gif

2017
At this point we spent a bunch of time to pin down our actual aesthetic by doing concept dioramas in engine to explore the colour palettes for each track.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/92d33ca297a2edd5a4fc5427c2d52d67ce2bd9ba.png

August 2017
Lakeside loop now redesigned and with a very rough art pass in the final style we'd end up going with. Besides the density and quality of assets the biggest thing missing here is reflections - which ended up becoming a big part of the final game's aesthetic. 
https://media.giphy.com/media/rM7xeBclw45xGTfkqs/giphy.gif

July 2018
At this point, with another pass on both the cars and the tracks, Lakeside Loop is starting to look a lot more like itself.
https://media.giphy.com/media/vZeyCXoFWAfHVjR5xm/giphy.gif

2018 Onwards
From this point much of the work was just taking our very rough tracks from this in May 2018:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/8600ad0adf0f15f83200cb2e0c959cd36cf83c52.jpg
To this in March 2020:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/be7aa3c474a72737cb642aed156400dd9d66d383.jpg

We've come a long way, and we couldn't have imagined what the final product was going to look like from the place we started.

We hope you are all enjoying it!

- Level 91 Entertainment

notes.title: Inertial Drift: 6 Things You Need to Know
notes.content:
Hello Fellow Drifters! 

It's great to see so many of you diving in and checking out everything that Inertial Drift has to offer (and we're seeing some seriously good times on those leaderboards 👀).

If you haven't already got behind the wheel (or behind the sticks...?), we've rounded up a few things you should know about Inertial Drift!

1. Inertial Drift has a unique twin-stick control scheme! 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/3c7487378bbe342c7bec04bbbb4f7a14418a522c.gif
The left stick is used for steering, while the right hand Drift Stick gives you independent control over your drift. Intuitive for new players and uniquely challenging for pros. What's more - each one of the 16 cars is a totally different beast, with unique characteristics to master. We hope you're up for a challenge. 
Find out more about the twin-stick controls here. 

2. There are 7 different event modes in which to perfect your craft! 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/7ba5e5f19b2aee4b53f68f9c865fb33591a91669.jpg 
Get competitive in a mix of races, head-to-heads, time trials and style showdowns!
Find out more about event types here.

3. You can customise your drifting experience 
https://media.giphy.com/media/ic6bmfPY7sQAjEqROM/giphy.gif
From car colour to audio and even inverting the twin-sticks(!) - Inertial Drift gives you plenty of options to drift exactly the way you want to. 
Find out more about customisation here. 

4. It has a *pretty sweet* animated Intro 
Inertial Drift's Animated Intro transports you to a 90s retro-future - where the cars are fiercely individual, the tracks are demanding and your opponents are ruthless. There's no better way to get in the mood for some drifting action, which is why you can enjoy the animation when you boot up the game. 
[previewyoutube=2s37jhq0jEM;full][/previewyoutube]

5. You don't just have to take our word for it. 
https://media.giphy.com/media/L4HhWo5siRc1npD950/giphy.gif
Inertial Drift is Eurogamer Recommended  and has received some incredible reviews from the gaming press - we're chuffed! 
Check out more Inertial Drift reviews here. 

6. You can play Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue for FREE!
A twin-stick control scheme is a brand new concept in the world of arcade racing. After a brief period of acclimatisation, we don't think you'll find a more satisfying way to race. However if you're feeling unsure, Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue is available for free on Steam and gives you a small taste of what you can expect in the full game! 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1302110/Inertial_Drift_Sunset_Prologue/

We keep saying it, but thanks again for your amazing support! If you have any questions about the game, feel free to reach out to us on Twitter at @PQubeIndies or @InertialDrift

- PQube & Level 91 Entertainment

notes.title: Drift Gyro: How the Twin Stick Controls Work in Inertial Drift
notes.content:
Inertial Drift's unique twin-stick control scheme gives you independent control over both steering and drifting, but how does the drift stick work?

It's all thanks to the Drift Gyro! 

Under the bonnet of every car there are two super-dense discs counter rotating at several thousand rpm. When you slam on the Drift Stick (right hand side!), power is diverted to the discs, tilting them off axis to create a torque on the car which kicks out the back end into a perfectly controlled slide. Here's a look at the Drift Gyro in action from Inertial Drift's Animated Intro: 

https://media.giphy.com/media/ib9dbuPmPNcIfDnIff/giphy.gif

"That doesn't make any sense!" we hear you say, well tell that to this physics teacher demonstrating the technique to his class:

https://media.giphy.com/media/dTuBk8PUaHRrmK45A6/giphy.gif

Don't worry though, understanding gyroscopic motion is not necessary to play Inertial Drift - and using the Drift Stick itself couldn't be easier! Push it right to drift right, push it left to drift left - it's that simple! You'll be drifting and cornering like a pro in no time at all!

https://media.giphy.com/media/YMSk973acENRVelhUk/giphy.gif

Experience the twin-stick control scheme for yourself when Inertial Drift releases on Steam this Friday! 

- PQube & Level 91 Entertainment

notes.title: How to customise your drifting experience in Inertial Drift
notes.content:
With just one week to go until you can get your hands on those twin-stick controls, we've put together a guide to help you experience Inertial Drift exactly the way you want to! 

Online Options
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/d814b3d1eba7ba772ed078c78572146d1fd88dda.gif
We recommend taking on Inertial Drift's gameplay modes to hone your craft before taking on other racers online. But who are we to stop you jumping online straight away? 

When playing online you'll have three car classes to choose from - Class C, Class B and Class A. The Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue will give you a small taste of what to expect from cars in the Class C and Class B category. As for Class A, well you'll have to find out for yourself... 

Get Sideways in Style
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/3a6c01d5f516d522e920655d936940360f050e40.gif
The cars in Inertial Drift are designed to evoke classic 90’s sports cars and tech - with futuristic qualities in keeping with the 90s-retro-future setting! Now, each car comes in a choice of 8 retro-inspired colourways as well as their original liveries. 

 Extensive Audio Options
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/a786f1e786062447098023992fd2796b8b809b61.gif
Every race location in Inertial Drift is accompanied by a bespoke soundtrack to match the environment and track type. It also changes dynamically according to what stage of the race you're in, making for an intense final sprint to the finish line!

You can also turn the soundtrack down and enjoy drifting to your favourite genre. 
I guess what we're tying to say is... *EUROBEAT INTENSIFIES*

You can also tweak elements such as tyre squeal, drift gyro effects and ambience to your liking. 

Gameplay Settings
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/2ebcfb7ff0df3da27c7045526a0c25ee45d96758.gif
Swap between KPH and MPH, toggle the rear view mirror and customise your drifting experience in the gameplay settings menu. You can even invert the twin-sticks! 

VFX 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/4ef63481be46f46a3873a1cf57acccd899052a4a.gif
Finally - you can also toggle and adjust a whole host of visual effects - including framerate, brightness and motion blur.

notes.title: Inertial Drift: Event Guide
notes.content:
From intense head-to-head races, to stylish solo cornering - Inertial Drift track events pack in plenty of variety.

Here's a closer look at what you can expect from Inertial Drift's seven different event modes:

- Practise - 
Practise makes... you know the rest. This mode keeps things simple - just you, your car and the road. It's the perfect way to get used to the handling of a brand new car for the first time, without having to compete for track-space with rivals. 

- Ghost Battle -
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/ad6963148dcb435ab4c7c4f25ac5e7895cddf009.png
Like practise mode, this is another great place to hone your craft, only this time you'll be racing against the ghosts of other players. Unlike in a full 1v1 race, Ghost Battles allow you a valuable insight into the way your opponents approach a track. Keep an eye out for their glowing skid-trails to help you study their lines and knock valuable seconds off your lap times.  

- Time Attack -  
Those of you who have already checked out the FREE Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue will be more than familiar with this mode. The objective is simple - record the fastest lap. Achieving it will be another matter... 

- Race - 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/dfba2af99b8d58d29790c5e3437e00244ba15b7d.jpg
This is what's it's all about. 
Intense, head-to-head racing in some of the most exciting cars you'll ever get behind the wheel of. All cars are fitted with the Phase Shift Impact Prevention System, so all you and your opponent need to do is focus on your lines. But don't make the mistake of thinking there won't be any crashes - the 20 tracks will demand total concentration and no shortage of skill to navigate safely. 

- Duel - 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/7ba5e5f19b2aee4b53f68f9c865fb33591a91669.jpg
As well as a traditional race, you can also take on drivers in Duel mode. Score points by putting distance between yourself and an opponent - and the first driver to fill up their bar wins! The race lead can swing frequently from one driver to another in Inertial Drift, so every second you can stay ahead is vital. 

- Endurance -
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/96834162bc77eebf1885fc179ec2557e2e7c8e5e.jpg
In this mode you'll race solo, attempting to reach each checkpoint before the timer runs out. Sure, the first lap might be easy enough - but how long will you be able to keep it up? 

- Style -
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/33ec52b2b8a35b2a30212e4cd86470db7c630c7d.jpg
Every drifter knows that it's not always about speed. This mode rewards those who are willing to take a risk in the pursuit of style. Race on the very limits of the track and earn points for nose skims, dirt drops and more. You can chain up moves for a greater reward, but be warned: a crash will result in them all being lost. 



Inertial Drift releases on 11th September 2020, and we can't wait for you to get your hands on the full game! 

- PQube & Level 91 Entertainment

notes.title: Track Focus: Downhill Rapids
notes.content:
While the Lakeside Loop is a great introductory track - Downhill Rapids throws you straight in at the deep end. 

The long, sweeping bends of the Lakeside Loop are the ideal place for a rookie racer to learn new techniques - but the hills above are home to a very different type of track. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/52d271de33b01b8127fe0b930ba9a01d8c94c118.jpg

Downhill Rapids is a technically demanding descent back down to water-level and will quickly put your newly learned techniques to the test. Expect a mixture of hairpin bends, sweeping corners and steep declines on your way down. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/f0199c23ee6200bf3b2bdc1dc03d5cece3820835.jpg 

Once you've made it back down to ground level, things don't get any easier! Pay close attention to the signage in the tunnel to avoid coming unstuck at a blind corner. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/ad7146f6eabc7466e5478334d70417b1fcb8eb0b.jpg

This may sound a little daunting, but choose a car you're familiar with for your first run and take it steady. And if you'd like to get some practise in, remember you can check out Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue for free! 

See you at the top of the pass! 

- PQube & Level 91 Entertainment

notes.title: Car Focus: Coda Chrono
notes.content:
When Inertial Drift releases later this summer there will be 16 fiercely individual cars to choose from! We take a closer look at the Coda Chrono:

Panned by critics due to its low power and low acceleration, Coda's Chrono has found a cult following among racers skilled enough to take advantage of its incredible top speed. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/4c8cb796a97b6a36925446d41038083d438be3c9.jpg

Inspired by the 90s Honda NSX, the Chrono is sporty, light and can be twitchy when it comes to handling. Conserving speed is essential to getting the most out of this car, but doing so can be quite a challenge... 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/8cc04e553ddd704fde60d96b124f7693009660fe.jpg

Challenging to get the most out of, but hugely rewarding for those who can - the Coda Chrono perfectly encompasses the incredibly satisfying racing experience that you can expect from Inertial Drift! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/b6070927dc202d96d817265dfaa7ba491412d17a.jpg

notes.title: Experience Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue Now!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=jiovZyMiEdc;full][/previewyoutube]

We're delighted to share that Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue is available to play right now on Steam for free!

CLICK HERE TO PLAY

This is very much a tiny taster of what’s to come, and we’ve been looking forward to being able to finally get something into your hands.

You see, Inertial Drift is by no means a standard racing game. Sure it looks like it in video or screenshots - but it is our hope that, when you touch it, when you feel the twin stick drifting mechanics, you’ll understand what sets Inertial Drift apart.

The goal was to take inspiration from the likes of Ridge Racer 4, where the thrill of the drift is such an integral part of those experiences and redefine, expand and explore those mechanics. To offer the player a new level of control and satisfaction from the simple act of drifting.

This is less a game about coming first, but rather the thrill of the chase, and the intensity of being pursued. But underneath all of that, the joy of bettering yourself. Of really getting to grips with the intricacies of your car, learning the tracks intimately and improving your times and your level of skill.

In Inertial Drift: Sunset Prologue we also wanted to highlight just how different the each individual car really is. When we say ‘fiercely individual’ we really mean it. Both the Coda Gecko and the Dragon will offer two very different styles of racing and handling – not just ‘a bit different’, but almost poles apart. This should give you some indication of what’s to come in the sheer diversity of the final roster. Each new car you use will offer the opportunity to re-learn how to race, how to drift and bring a completely new level of enjoyment to each track.

We hope you enjoy the purity of the racing experience in Inertial Drift, to revel in the high skill ceiling some of these cars have to offer. We’re really looking forward to seeing (and competing with!) your best times in Sunset Prologue and, as ever, we welcome your feedback in the community pages.

If you have enjoyed Sunset Prologue, do please drop by the main page for Inertial Drift and wishlist us here. Your support is very much appreciated.

See you on the leaderboards!

- Level 91 and PQube

notes.title: Development Update - New features to help you learn from your opponents
notes.content:
In Inertial Drift, you'll need to learn from your competitors as well as compete with them! Studying the lines that others are using could give you an edge in those intense 1v1 races, and the team have recently introduced two new upgrades to help you do just that!


Break Trails That Hang in the Air 
[previewyoutube=csaVrki3YIw;full][/previewyoutube]

If you're already familiar with Inertial Drift, you'll know that the break trails from your car and your opponent's car hang in the air for a short while. Notice your opponent acing a tricky corner? Study their break trails to see exactly where they applied and released the breaks!

A new proximity based fade sees the trails fade-out as you cover the same ground, allowing you to replicate your opponent's throttle & break timings in real-time. 


Glowing Skid Trails 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36398504/ad6963148dcb435ab4c7c4f25ac5e7895cddf009.png

Another recent addition comes in the form of glowing skid trails. Racing ghosts - whether your own or somebody else's - is another invaluable opportunity to hone your craft. These new glowing skid-trails for ghosts make it even easier to study their lines. 


Remember, each car in Inertial Drift is different! Simply copying what your opponent does is no guaruntee of success...


Thanks and stay tuned for more!
- PQube & Level 91 Entertainment



Find out more about Inertial Drift at http://pqube.co.uk/inertial-drift
